figures.title: Independent head and tail wrap
figures.caption: Two queued records span the physical end of the eight-byte ring.
figures.alt: Five annotated details after command index three. The next instruction is operation ready. Return status is zero and encoded size is four. Descriptor head four, tail three, used seven and capacity eight accompany the full ring pointer. At physical indices four through seven and zero through two, records contain x y and hexadecimal 7f 80 ff. Old byte 43 at index three is unoccupied. Output contains the earlier popped A B C.

figures.title: Exact fit uses every ring byte
figures.caption: An exact-fit record fills all eight bytes even though head and tail are equal.
figures.alt: Five annotated details after command index eight. Return status is zero and encoded size eight. Descriptor head and tail both four, used eight, capacity eight. Prefix seven at ring index four precedes payload 00 01 02 7f 80 fe ff across the end. The destination for a later pop remains filled with 55.

figures.title: Short destination leaves a record queued
figures.caption: A six-byte destination leaves the seven-byte record queued for a larger-destination retry.
figures.alt: Five annotated details after command index ten. Signed return status minus two and required payload length seven signal a short destination. Descriptor remains head four, tail four, used eight, capacity eight. Ring contents are identical to the full state. The prospective output payload remains seven bytes of 55, with no failed-call stores.
